quote.text: We shape our tools, and thereafter our tools shape us.
quote.author: Father John Culkin, 1967, glossing Marshall McLuhan

macro.title: What It Means for VWRA, Global Bonds, Gold & BTC

stories.kicker: The Atelier · Buy It Once — No. 6 · Claw Machines
stories.headline: The Most Honest Machine in the Arcade Is the One Everybody Calls Rigged
stories.dek: And both halves of that sentence are true. The cabinet is simple; the money hides in one setting. Buy the machine, and for the first time the setting is yours.

stories.kicker: The Rabbit Hole · The Invitation — Reef Aquariums
stories.headline: A Miniature Ocean, and the Tank Is the Cheapest Part
stories.dek: You are not keeping fish. You are running a slice of tropical sea inside three narrow numbers — and the corals, which are the point, will make you obsess over every one of them.

stories.headline: A Tripled Tax, a New Way Home, and the Refund You'll Now Chase at the Gate
stories.dek: What actually changed on the departures board since the last weekend: Japan gets pricier to leave and trickier to shop tax-free, Madrid joins the map, and the causeway's little train enters its home stretch.

stories.headline: The Richest Man China Ever Made, and Then Unmade
stories.dek: A Shenzhen court gave Hui Ka Yan life and took the whole fortune — a clean end to the Evergrande man, five years after his company fell on more than three hundred billion dollars of debt. The country he built in is still living in the wreckage.

stories.headline: The Rally the Household Is Actually Waiting On
stories.dek: Tomorrow night the Prime Minister stands up to talk about the cost of raising children. For a family with a twelve-year-old, the question is whether the help reaches the years that are about to get expensive — or stops at the pre-school gate.

stories.headline: A Model Too Good to Ship, and a Toolkit That Just Got Better
stories.dek: The open-weights world had a two-speed week: a frontier Chinese model held back at the gate over what it can hack, and — quietly, usefully — a free toolkit that makes the model already on your rig run better.

stories.kicker: The Kit · The Battery You Can Replace
stories.headline: Sennheiser Builds a Flagship Earbud You Are Allowed to Keep
stories.dek: The MOMENTUM True Wireless 5 puts a user-replaceable cell in both the buds and the case — a small screw driven straight into the category's dirtiest secret, the two-year death by dead battery.

stories.kicker: The Good Life · The Watch a Student Never Made
stories.headline: A Magazine's Founder Builds the Watch of a 1932 Counterfactual
stories.dek: Wei Koh spent twenty years writing about watchmaking. His answer to "what if a forgotten prodigy had stayed" is two balance wheels, a planetary differential, and a Singapore retail partner already lined up.

stories.headline: A Magic Tree, a Gold Album, and Two Old Names Reaching Back
stories.dek: Enid Blyton's eighty-seven-year-old tree finally reaches American screens as an unplug-the-family fantasy, and Weezer swings, one more time, for the record it made when this reader was in his twenties.

stories.kicker: The Family Desk · The Ban She Barely Noticed
stories.headline: A Wall Went Up Around Social Media. A Twelve-Year-Old Walked Around It.
stories.dek: The first hard data on Australia's under-16 ban is in, and the uncomfortable finding is age-shaped: the youngest kids, the ones the ban most wants to protect, changed their habits least.

stories.kicker: The Macro Desk · The Debasement Bid
stories.headline: A Fed That Won't Talk, a Treasury Buying Its Own Bond
stories.dek: The regime has quietly flipped from the one most readers assume. The debate is not about cuts — it is about a possible hike, from a chair who has stopped telling markets anything. That is why gold and bitcoin rose together this week.

stories.headline: Zone 2 Was Never Magic. Guard the One Session That Is.
stories.dek: A 2025 review takes the halo off the longevity crowd's favourite pace. The base still earns its place — but the number that actually tracks how long you live moves at a harder effort.

stories.kicker: The Diary · The Stadium Autumn Returns
stories.headline: One Free Festival Is on Right Now — Then October's Wall of Stadium Nights
The Little Red Search Engine
stories.dek: A Chinese lifestyle app has quietly stopped being a feed young Southeast Asians scroll and become the search engine they trust — the thing they consult before they eat, travel or buy. Whoever owns that moment owns default reality. In two plural societies, it is now a Chinese app.
